record_notes.DCP-LETT-1274: December 3 with supplied 1849 year. Introductory request prompted by missing John Morris letter identifying Fitch Chalk specimen; not a Fitch incoming prompt. Requests loan for weeks and provenance of Chalk, gives postal and carrier options. Already holds Bowerbank/Wood/Buckman/Sowerby specimens; Copenhagen lot only on its way. Intended Ray Society monograph includes recent and fossil at this time; later division between Ray and Palaeontographical societies must not overwrite stated plan. Eventual species identifications in footnotes are later, not already known.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1288: January 6 with supplied 1850 year. Renews request for original Pollicipes and any separate valves, now has 40–50 specimens but has given up Copenhagen lot. Intended week of comparison and promised acknowledgment/postage reimbursement are not evidence the Fitch lot has arrived. Later thanks and intact associated-valve value are future developments. No preserved Fitch agreement supplies an incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1290: January 10 with supplied 1850 year. Actual Fitch note and specimens received by this letter, only glanced at; one flat valve damaged, another chalk matrix damaged without valve injury. Repair hoped, not yet completed. Initial tentative identification relates specimen to S. quadratum/rutilum and believes Pollicipes maximus; later fossula decision remains later. Asks permission for Sowerby drawing and proposes London around 20th, contingent on wife confinement and consent. Promises not to touch chalk. Missing note/loan permission cannot be reconstructed; later January 15 birth is not January 10 knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1291: January 15 with supplied 1850 year. Responds to missing Fitch forgiving accident and offering duplicate; 13 fragments now repaired and scientifically usable. British Museum donation is intended after completion, fossil publisher only possible. Enumerates provisional identifications including fossula, sulcatum, maximum and new Pollicipes, describes danger of naming separate valves as species and asks for more. Curved-valve sketch with x tip broken off is integral to identification, not decorative. Reports box crushed rather than jar injury. Reopened P11 requests explicit yes/no to clear hidden side, no permission yet. P12 brother house full and wife confinement delay travel. P11–13 manuscript postscript is actually bound with January 28 letter but editor assigns here; retain editorial relocation and uncertain exact completion, not automatic January 28 or independently certain January 15 for every line.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1295: Wednesday assigned January 23, 1850. Acknowledges another note and specimens, several new valves. Two slightly broken and a third more damaged; upside-down specimen was useless in matrix but now detached and potentially repairable. Specific shipment differs from January 10 lot; no accumulated single arrival date. Promises fuller report. Incoming note is absent, physical specimens are not a textual prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1298: Monday evening assigned January 28, 1850 through neighboring letters. Latest Fitch lot arrived safely; one intermediate specimen confirms maximum and sulcatum as varieties rather than species, more valuable than a new species. Two new species from Morris arrived by same morning post, separate shipment. Five named forms listed with maximum varieties sulcatum/solidulum; four called new. Raw HTML splits list and includes diag/ramme artefacts, duplicate I numbering and S. Sowerby slip; preserve original versus editorial correction rather than silently normalizing. Productus later renamed angelini, not already that name here. Missing note conveys twenty years collecting and ill health. No preserved incoming letter or known exact receipt for every earlier lot.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1299: February 1 with supplied 1850 year. Reports five workdays lost to illness and 2½ hours worked on other days, confirmed MathML rather than 212. About 200 specimens, eleven described, at least twelve more expected; numbers are current progress, not final totals. Next Wednesday drawing visit planned, longer loan requested under silence convention and return labels promised. No proof silent permission or completed travel at this date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1301: Tuesday assigned February 5, 1850. Requests permission to soak/clear upside-down concave specimen, explicitly does not know its valve or whether species new; diagram marks concavity. Distinguish this new permission from earlier permission already granted for carina extra side, which has now been exposed successfully and is to be figured. Reports new Pollicipes from Fitch and two new Flower Scalpellum. Reopened P4 thanks another Fitch letter just received, after main text composition. Later named angelini is future nomenclature. No preserved permission letter or latest note; do not substitute own January 15 request as incoming.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1302: Wednesday assigned February 6, 1850. Further specimens arrived before immediate intended London departure; one cracked, otherwise safe and some new things. This is a new arrival acknowledgment, not proof earlier promised journey completed or a full incoming letter. Prior day offer inferred in apparatus is not surviving verbatim prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1313: March 17 with supplied 1850 year. All current Fitch specimens described but second pass still needed; Sowerby reports about half drawn and remaining delivery is planned in a week or ten days. Palaeontographical Society has agreed to publish, not already printed. Reopened postscript thanks many specimens preventing errors and asks for further fragments. Later published maximum-variety argument helps interpret significance but cannot be substituted as contemporary quote or additional incoming source. Missing Sowerby progress report and Society decision lack available text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1315: Saturday conjectural April 13, 1850 based on Sowerby visit relationship. Some drawn specimens returned to Darwin, others delivered to artist; none thereby proved returned to Fitch. Darwin says ready for press but plates delayed, not actual press until future 1851. Sowerby cleared chalk without authorization, reveals possible Terebratula or Crania new to him; reported artist interpretation, not Darwin new-species determination. Foreign-species job is editorial possibility. Source describes historical permission overreach; no agent action authorized by it.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1325: May 5 with supplied 1850 year. Two more specimens safely received, valves new to Fitch collection but unsuitable as basis for specific names. New-to-collection does not mean new species. No incoming cover text preserved and no precise arrival time beyond acknowledgment.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1366: November 3 with supplied 1850 year. Explicitly answers missing Fitch inquiry over long retention, states delay caused by engravings and asks continued loan. Artist progress partly known, much merely hoped; prior engagements/Botanic Garden routine are hypothesized causes. Council members also urged progress. No completed plates or returned collection yet, and prior permission cannot be inferred to extend indefinitely. Missing Fitch query and Sowerby reports preclude a textual pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1369: November 11 with supplied 1850 year. Fitch note and Sowerby complaint response arrived by same post; one of five plates perfect, not all five. Sowerby reports house demolition as chief cause, a newly supplied explanation rather than Darwin earlier knowledge. Darwin plans further pressure and says Fitch will soon demand specimens back. Pamphlet received but title is editorial possibility, not certain identification or proof read. Declines additional specimens. Sowerby is James de Carle; later George Brettingham Jr work on other volumes does not change authorship of this report.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1376: Monday, conjectural December 1850. Several specimens with excellent drawings back from Sowerby, several still retained, all plate positions arranged but proof verification pending. Promises Fitch return in week completed proofs checked; no actual return date follows. Dating rationale places between November 11, 1850 and January 24, 1851, with completed illustrations by middle January only described in later context. Preferred December month is not independently established; keep exact-date and active-period-boundary hold rather than exclude possible early 1851. No fresh incoming prompt or complete proofs supplied here.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Long crescent-like curved valve outline with parallel contours, x and literal tip broken off at the right end. Preserve asymmetry and damaged-tip qualification with body identification.

Narrow elongated valve outline labeled concave inside, with pointed top and irregular lower end. Illustrates upward-facing concavity of a still-unidentified valve; do not label as an identified species.

reading_method: Fresh independent full reading of fifteen targets, including complete apparatus and bibliography; both inline figures visually inspected. Raw MathML 1299 and split list 1298 checked. Preserved incoming search finds no Fitch/Morris letter or current James de Carle Sowerby letter; older George Brettingham Sowerby records do not supply these current missing inputs.
